title: Characterizing the Prompted vs. Unprompted Sycophancy Gap
original_idea: Design paired questions where the false premise is embedded in the question itself vs. introduced after the model initially answers correctly. Measure whether unprompted sycophancy rates differ from prompted ones, and whether the mechanisms differ.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Unprompted sycophancy is more insidious and harder to detect. Characterizing this gap is a critical safety contribution.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing paired questions and measuring rates is straightforward. Multi-turn setup for prompted variant adds some complexity but manageable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused comparison on one dimension with paired questions on 1-2 models. Clear experimental design. Well within 30hrs.

novelty.reasoning: The distinction between different sycophancy types is an active research area. 'Sycophancy Is Not One Thing' (2025) causally separates sycophantic agreement from sycophantic praise, showing distinct mechanisms. ELEPHANT (2025) introduces 'social sycophancy' measuring implicit sycophancy beyond direct agreement. 'When Truth Is Overridden' (2025) investigates internal origins. However, the specific prompted-vs-unprompted framing (false premise in question vs. introduced after correct answer) as a paired experimental design is not directly addressed by existing work. The mechanistic comparison adds value, though the general direction is partially explored.
